text: Allostasis, unlike classical homeostasis, involves predictively adjusting the set points of regulated variables in anticipation of expected demands (for example, the pre-dawn rise in cortisol before waking).
explanation: True. Allostasis, proposed by Sterling and Eyer, is 'stability through change': set points are proactively shifted in anticipation of upcoming demands, as with anticipatory heart-rate increases before exercise or the morning cortisol peak. Classical homeostasis instead reactively defends fixed set points through negative feedback.
